data.cultural_impact: The name "Sual" holds a unique cultural significance as it is derived from the Arabic language's root "sawl" which means "cool water." Naming a child "Sual" could be considered symbolic of wishing for blessings and comforting sustenance in the form of knowledge, wealth, and relationships, just as one finds relief and quenching with cool water. It could also be a nod to lineage and tradition, being rooted in the rich cultural heritage of the Middle East.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name "Sual" carries powerful connotations for Muslims, reminding us of the importance of seeking knowledge as a vital means to quench our spiritual thirst. In Islam, this pursuit of knowledge is continually encouraged and even considered a personal obligation. The name serves as a beautiful reminder of the teachings found within the holy Quran: "So remember Me; I will remember you. Be grateful to Me and do not reject faith." (Al Quran 2:152) Through this name, Sual, an individual is constantly reminded to seek knowledge, be grateful, and have faith in the Divine will. Ultimately, this name serves as a reminder to be in pursuit of spiritual growth, enlightenment, and closeness to the Creator.

historical_references.reference: The Islamic city of Sual was a significant port city in the 15th century. It was an important trading post for the Maluku Islands and the spice trade between Southeast Asia and the Middle East. Sual was ruled by the Sultanate of Ternate, and was a major contributor to the economic prosperity of the region.

historical_references.reference: Sual was also known as a center of Islamic scholarship and learning during the 17th century. It was a major hub for the dissemination of Islamic knowledge throughout Southeast Asia, with many scholarly figures residing there and attracting students from all over the region.
